title: 2020年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics lately. In early May, London's Boring Conference celebrated seven years of delighting in dullness. At this event, people flocked to talks about weather, traffic jams and vending-machine sounds, among other sleep-inducing topics.

P2 What, exactly, is everybody studying? One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." But how can you quantify a person's boredom level and compare it with someone else's? In 1986, psychologists introduced the Boredom Proneness Scale, designed to measure an individual's overall tendency to feel bored. By contrast, the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, developed in 2008, measures a person's feelings of boredom in a given situation.

P3 Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. In fact, many of us would choose pain over boredom. One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self- administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. Researching this phenomenon, another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films, during which they could self-administer electric shocks. The bored volunteers shocked themselves more and harder than the sad or neutral ones did.

P4 But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. An early study gave participants abundant time to complete problem-solving and word-association exercises. Once all the obvious answers were exhausted, participants gave more and more inventive answers to combat boredom. A British study took these findings one step further, asking subjects to complete a creative challenge (coming up with a list of alternative uses for a household item). One group of subjects did a boring activity first, while the others went straight to the creative task. Those whose boredom pumps had been primed were more productive.

P5 In our always-connected world, boredom may be a hard-to-define state, but it is a fertile one. Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea.

questions.q: When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?
options: When they don't have the chance to do what they want.
When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.
When they engage in some routine activities.
questions.explain:
【判型】When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?是 When 引导的事实型疑问句，且明确以according to an accepted psychological definition限定信息来源，答案应是原文定义句的客观转述。

【拆句】题干主干是 When are people likely to experience boredom，主句问的是「时间/情 境」；后置介词短语according to an accepted psychological definition为状语，限定答 案来源必须是「公认的心理学定义」，不是作者本人观点或常识。

【定位】One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." 无聊在心理学上一个被广为接受的定义是「想去从事一项令人满足的活动，却无法去做时的 那种不快体验」。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity ↔ don't have the chance to do what they want When they don't have the chance to do what they want.把原文定义句的两个核心成 分「有意愿」与「被阻止」一一保留，且未添加任何原文未给出的限定，是定义句的最 忠实改写。 B) 无中生有 When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.把场景限定到「学习材 料」，但原文定义未提学习场景，纯属添油加醋。 C) 偷换概念 When they experience something unpleasant.把原文里的「不快体验」拿出来当条 件，可原文 distasteful experience 描述的是无聊本身（结果），不是触发无聊的条 件，因果倒置。 D) 与原文相反 When they engage in some routine activities.把无聊触发条件描述为「在做日常 活动」，可原文定义明确强调「想做却做不成」，主体是「未能从事」而非「正在 从事」。 作者认为无聊会导致什么? A) 决心。 B) 专注。 C) 精神退化。 D) 有害行为。

questions.q: What does the author say boredom can lead to?
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say boredom can lead to?是 What 引导的事实问句，问的是「无 聊会导致什么」，是对原文具体陈述的转述。

【拆句】句子主干 What ... boredom can lead to，是宾语前置的特殊疑问句；what 是 lead to 的 宾语，问的是「后果」。句中嵌入does the author say并非考点，仅说明信息来源是作者 陈述，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. 无聊与多种行为问题相关，包括驾驶时心不在焉、不动脑子地乱吃东西、过量饮酒以及嗜赌 成瘾。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Determination.意为「决心」，原文从未提到无聊会让人变得有决心；整段讨论的全是 负面后果，与正向心理品质毫无关联。 B) 与原文相反 Concentration.意为「专注」，与原文inattentive driving描述的「分心驾驶」恰好相 反；无聊导致的是注意力涣散，不是专注。 C) 过度推断 Mental deterioration.意为「精神/智力衰退」，是把原文里的具体行为问题进一步推到 「精神层面退化」的程度，原文未提任何精神疾病或认知衰退后果。 D) ✓ 正确 behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling ↔Harmful conduct. Harmful conduct.既保留了 behavior=conduct 的词汇对应，又用 harmful 准确概括 了那四个具体后果的共同属性，是对原文罗列最贴切的总括式改写。 一组心理学家在实验中有什么发现? A) 志愿者更愿意看一部乏味的电影,而不是独自坐着思考。 B) 许多志愿者选择伤害自己,而不是忍受无聊。 C) 男性志愿者比女性更能抵御无聊的影响。 D) 许多志愿者无法忍受超过十五分钟的无聊。

questions.q: What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?
options: Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.
Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.
Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.
Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?问的是具体实验 的结论事实，需回到该实验描述句做同义比对，属典型细节题。 48. What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment? A) Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating. B) Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom. C) Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females. D) Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.

【拆句】主干 What is the finding，主系表结构；of one team of psychologists 修饰 finding，in their experiment 进一步限定研究情境。三层修饰只是把范围限到「那个团队那次实验的结 论」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. 一组心理学家发现，三分之二的男性与四分之一的女性宁愿对自己施加电击，也不愿独自静 坐沉思 15 分钟。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.把后文另 一项实验「看无聊片时电击自己」（another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films）的实验对象混进来——这是另一团队的研究，对应另一 题的结论，不是本题考的实验。 B) ✓ 正确 would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes ↔ Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom. Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.既保留 了原文比较结构两端的方向，又把具体动作恰当上位化，是对实验发现的最忠实概括。 C) 与原文相反 Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.把男女 比例的差异解读成「男性更能抗无聊」，可原文是「三分之二男性 vs 四分之一女性都选 择了电击」——男性选择电击的比例反而更高，意味着男性更难忍无聊，结论方向完全 相反。 D) 过度推断 Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.把 15 分钟当成志愿者能忍耐的上限，可原文只是说「实验设定独坐 15 分钟」，并未测出志愿 者的耐受阈值——结论从实验时长推到「忍耐极限」，多迈了一步。 作者为什么说无聊并非全是坏事? A) 它刺激记忆。 B) 它为放松提供了时间。 C) 它可能促进创造性思维。 D) 它可能促进自主学习。

questions.q: Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?问作者给出的理由，原文转折句后必紧 跟解释，答案是该解释句的转述。 49. Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad? A) It stimulates memorization. B) It allows time for relaxation. C) It may promote creative thinking. D) It may facilitate independent learning.

【拆句】句首 Why 引出原因；主谓 does the author say 套着宾语从句 boredom isn't all bad。从 句用 isn't all bad（部分否定）而非 isn't bad，表示「并非完全是坏事」，暗示后面一定有 正面意义的展开。

【定位】But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. 但无聊也并非全是坏事。通过促进自省与遐想，它能激发创造力。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It stimulates memorization.说无聊会刺激记忆，但原文谈的是 self-reflection、 daydreaming、creativity，全程没有 memory/memorization 这一概念。 B) 偷换概念 It allows time for relaxation.把无聊的好处概括为「有时间放松」，可原文明确说的是 促进自省与遐想进而激发创造力，重点是「创造产出」而非「身心放松」。 C) ✓ 正确 it can spur creativity ↔It may promote creative thinking. It may promote creative thinking.两端的动词（spur→promote）和名词 （creativity→creative thinking）都做了精准的同义替换，且未引入任何超出原文的限 定，是理由句的最忠实改写。 D) 过度推断 It may facilitate independent learning.把好处推到「促进自主学习」，但原文谈的是 创造力，而非学习或独立学习；从「自我反思」推到「独立学习」多走了一步。 作者建议人们在面对具有挑战性的问题时应该做什么? A) 停止闲散,放眼大局。 B) 解锁自己的智能手机。 C) 环顾四周寻找刺激。 D) 允许自己有一些时间感到无聊。

questions.q: What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?
options: Allow oneself some time to be bored.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?问的 是作者给出的具体行动建议，是原文建议句的客观转述，未要求推断。

【拆句】主干 What does the author suggest one do，其中 one do 是 suggest 后省略 that 与 should 的虚拟语气从句；when faced with a challenging problem 是过去分词作时间状 语，相当于 when one is faced with ...，意为「当面对难题时」。 50. What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem? A) Stop idling and think big. B) Unlock one's smartphone. C) Look around oneself for stimulation. D) Allow oneself some time to be bored.

【定位】Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea. 看油漆变干，看水烧开，或者至少先把手机放下一会儿，你就可能解开下一个大点子。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Stop idling and think big.让人停止闲散、去想大事，可原文恰恰建议你 idle 一会儿 （看油漆干、看水开就是 idling）——方向完全相反。 B) 与原文相反 Unlock one's smartphone.让人解锁手机，可原文建议的是put away your smartphone，即放下手机；动作方向完全相反。 C) 与原文相反 Look around oneself for stimulation.让人四处寻找刺激，可原文建议恰好是减少刺激 （看油漆、看水开都是极低刺激场景，放下手机是切断刺激源）——方向相反。 D) ✓ 正确 Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while ↔ Allow oneself some time to be bored. Allow oneself some time to be bored.既呼应了尾段「主动放空」的具体动作，又与 全文「无聊能激发创造力」的主旨完全对齐，是对建议句最贴切的上位概括。
